## Understand language models, one mechanism at a time

A progressive path connecting intuition, mathematics, code, and experimental evidence. High-level pages explain how components work together; concept pages go deeper into one idea and link to its equations, references, and implementation status.

The long-term goal is to understand and build a small decoder-only autoregressive language model, using inspectable components and tests. Sebastian Raschka's repository is a major source and comparison point, not a table of contents to copy or evidence that the corresponding steps are already implemented here.

## Suggested path

1. **Maths applied to LLMs** — follow logits through the training loss and gradients without duplicating a general mathematics course.
2. **Attention and Transformers** — queries, keys, values, scores, softmax, positional information (including RoPE), and causal masking.
3. **Data and the autoregressive objective** — tokenization, input-target shifting, and next-token prediction.
4. **Model and training** — blocks, optimization, validation, generation, and evaluation.
5. **Critical notes** — examine assumptions, counterexamples, and the limitations of metrics and representations.

This path describes the learning structure, not the implementation status of every component. The [detailed learning path](https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab/blob/main/docs/learning-path.md), [full curriculum and source-coverage plan](https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab/blob/main/docs/full-curriculum-plan.md), and [roadmap](https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab/blob/main/docs/roadmap.md) define the learning stages, how sources fit the project, and validation criteria respectively.

## How to use the sources

Different resources serve different purposes: an animation can build intuition, a research paper establishes the original formulation, official documentation specifies API behaviour, and tested code checks a defined property. Cross-check them rather than treating them as interchangeable.

- [Sebastian Raschka — reading recommendations](https://github.com/rasbt/LLMs-from-scratch/blob/main/ch01/reading-recommendations.md): first read for the big picture, second read with code, then critical reuse in a project.
- [3Blue1Brown — Transformers, the tech behind LLMs](https://www.3blue1brown.com/lessons/gpt/): visual intuition for data flow and LLM components.
- [Jay Alammar — The Illustrated Transformer](https://jalammar.github.io/illustrated-transformer/) and [The Illustrated GPT-2](https://jalammar.github.io/illustrated-gpt2/): visual walkthroughs of architectures; distinguish the original encoder-decoder Transformer from a decoder-only GPT.
- [Hugging Face — LLM Course](https://huggingface.co/learn/llm-course/): a structured supplement for concepts, tools, and models.

Formal references and further resources are collected in the [annotated bibliography](../references.qmd). For each page, mathematical and technical claims should be connected to an appropriate source; pedagogical links support understanding but do not replace definitions, assumptions, or derivations.
